claims.text: Instrumented nanoindentation can assess the small-scale mechanical behavior of FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloys.
Local mechanical-property variations in FeNiCrMn correlate with microstructural features such as grain size.
The initial FeNiCrMn alloy has a fine, homogeneous grain structure.
Instrumented nanoindentation produces load-displacement curves from which hardness and elastic modulus can be derived.
Grain size influences dislocation nucleation and propagation in FeNiCrMn.
Subtle local compositional variations influence dislocation nucleation and propagation in FeNiCrMn.
Nanoindentation applies sufficiently high local stress to activate dislocation mechanisms.
Differences in localized microstructure produce variations in nanoindentation load-displacement response, hardness, and elastic modulus.
Regions with finer grains are expected to have higher hardness.
Regions with finer grains are expected to have higher elastic modulus.
Regions with a more uniform microstructure are expected to have higher hardness and elastic modulus.
Nanoindentation can detect local mechanical-property variations that bulk mechanical tests may average out.
Significant phase segregation or secondary precipitation could obscure the correlation between grain structure and mechanical response.
Sample processing can affect the measured nanoindentation responses.
